items.quote: identified through converging forensic evidence as "Iaman Informant" (username: informant, email: iaman.informant@nist.gov)
items.why: The name and address match the key (Q20), and the report ties them to the Outlook OST references, the profile name and the resignation-letter filename.

items.quote: hostname "informant-PC," running Windows 7 64-bit in the Eastern Standard Time zone
items.why: Windows 7 64-bit is right, but the report never states the Ultimate edition (Q3) or the standalone WORKGROUP configuration.

items.quote: RM1's exFAT partition (volume label "Authorized USB," volume serial 5c75-4d3e)
items.why: exFAT and the "Authorized USB" label match Section 2, but SanDisk Cruzer Fit and S/N 4C530012450531101593 are absent, and the report wrongly gives RM1 a second FAT32 partition.

items.quote: RM2 (IAMAN $_@, FAT32, Volume ID: 0xb4d85399)
items.why: FAT32 and the label are right, but the SanDisk Cruzer Fit identity and serial 4C530012550531106501 (Q22) are not reported.

items.quote: the subject burned data to the CD-R (RM3, volume label "IAMAN CD") in nine UDF VAT sessions
items.why: CD-R with UDF is correct, and the 20:54-20:57 UTC burn matches the key's 16:54-16:58 local, but the UDF format time of 2015-03-24 16:53:17 local (20:53:17 UTC, Q33) is never given.

items.quote: Between 16:52:08 and 16:52:20 UTC, five classified Office documents were copied to this partition with their original filenames intact
items.why: These five files are the authorized company copies on RM#1 (Section 2 note 5; Section 3 copies them FROM RM#1 to the PC on 2015-03-24 09:40), so presenting them as exfiltrated to USB contradicts the key, whose USB leakage is the 17 files on RM#2 (Q55, Q59).

items.quote: Contains same data but deliberately disguised with false filenames and extensions (see masquerading finding).
items.why: All 17 false names on RM2, with their true formats and sizes (e.g. winter_whether_advisory.zip = PPTX, 16,381,123 bytes), match Q53/Q55 and are backed by masquerade detection and a file-size mapping.

items.quote: followed by the CCleaner v5.04 installer (ccsetup504.exe) at 14:57:56 UTC. Eraser was executed at 15:12:28 UTC for secure file deletion
items.why: The installer and execution times (14:50:14, 14:57:56, 15:12:28 and 15:15:50 UTC) equal the key's 10:50:14-11:15:50 local entries (Q11, Q52) and are supported by UserAssist, ShimCache and MFT evidence.

items.quote: The subject researched "information+leakage+cases," "how+to+leak+a+secret," "intellectual+property+theft," and "data+leakage+methods" before executing the campaign.
items.why: The leakage and anti-forensics searches are correctly recovered with bulk_extractor, but the narrative puts the "anti-forensic+tools", "ccleaner" and "eraser" searches on March 23, while Q16 dates them to 2015-03-25 10:46-10:47.

items.quote: Google Drive was installed at approximately 20:01:53 UTC, with ShimCache confirming googledrivesync.exe was executed.
items.why: The installation is evidenced and agrees with Q10, but the report misses the actual 2015-03-23 16:32 upload and sharing of happy_holiday.jpg and do_u_wanna_build_a_snow_man.mp3 (Q30, Q59) and leaves cloud exfiltration as a hedged possibility.

items.quote: Apple iCloud was also installed (icloudsetup.exe appeared in UserAssist), though no definitive evidence of iCloud data synchronization was found.
items.why: icloudsetup.exe in UserAssist, the Bonjour install at 20:00:56 UTC and the "apple icloud" search agree with Q10, Q11, Q16 and Q29.

items.quote: The USBSTOR driver was last written at 13:37:59 UTC
items.why: The report gives a registry LastWrite that matches RM#1's 09:38 local reconnection, but it uses no EVTX System-log events and gives no per-device connection times, such as RM#2 at 09:58:32 local (Q22).

items.quote: The earliest evidence of exfiltration dates to Sunday, February 15, 2015. At 16:51:38 UTC, the Secret Project Data directory structure was created on RM1's exFAT partition
items.why: The key has no activity on Feb 15: RM#1 is the company's authorized storage device (Section 2), the leak begins after the conspirator's offer with e-mails from 2015-03-23, and Q59 lists only e-mail, Google Drive, RM#2 and the CD-R as leakage methods.

items.quote: 15:18:36Z: Software\...\Run key emptied (by CCleaner removing startup entries)
items.why: The key says CCleaner was launched and closed after doing nothing (Section 3, 2015-03-25 11:15) and was uninstalled at 11:18, which contradicts the report's statements that it performed "system trace cleaning" and emptied the Run key.

items.quote: All 17 masqueraded documents are deleted orphan files.
items.why: The deletion on RM2 FAT32 is shown through orphaned entries, but no deletion time or method is established (key: quick format at 17:02 local, Q54), and the only times given are FAT creation times labelled UTC.

items.quote: The same three email addresses embedded within the document content — Eric_P._Lauer@omb.eop.gov, wayne.longman@att.net, and mmun@loc.gov — appeared at proportional disc offsets on both RM2 and RM3
items.why: The report ties RM3's 17 documents to the Secret Project set by file size and by embedded government content (OMB, LoC, govdocs references), consistent with Q56 and the Govdocs1 seed files.

items.quote: E:\Secret Project Data\design\winter_whether_advisory.zip [16381123] — the user specifically opened the masqueraded file and explored its ppt\ subdirectory
items.why: The opened file and its ppt subfolder match Q26, but the report names only drive E: on a USB device and never attributes the access to RM2.

items.quote: where the subject navigated through the complete directory tree including Secret Project Data, Common Data, and Past Projects subdirectories
items.why: The traversed share and V: paths match Q27 with shellbag evidence, but the narrative dates first access to 2015-03-22 14:52:22 UTC, while the key has 2015-03-23 16:23-16:24 local (Q24, Q27).

items.quote: Bulk extractor recovered an Outlook contact entry for "spy" with email address spy.conspirator@nist.gov from the PC's disk image.
items.why: The report finds only a contact entry and says no messages were recovered, while the key documents a full e-mail exchange, including an attachment and Drive links (Q21, Q45).

items.quote: Between 09:59:26 and 10:00:18 UTC, seventeen masqueraded copies of the Secret Project Data documents were created
items.why: The report never notes that FAT32 stores local time and labels these times UTC, whereas the key's copy to RM#2 is at 09:59 local (13:59 UTC).

other_false_positives.quote: RM1 was configured with two distinct partitions to enable plausible deniability.
other_false_positives.why: Section 2 describes RM#1 as an exFAT "Authorized USB" volume; the FAT32 "IAMAN $_@" volume is RM#2, a separate device with its own serial (Q22).

other_false_positives.quote: seventeen masqueraded copies of the Secret Project Data documents were created on both RM1's FAT32 partition and RM2
other_false_positives.why: Q55 and Q59 show the masqueraded files were copied only to RM#2; RM#1 was only a source of files copied to the PC (Section 3, 2015-03-23 14:39 and 2015-03-24 09:40).

other_false_positives.quote: The creation of redundant copies across three physically separate media — two USB devices and one CD-R — represents a deliberate strategy to ensure the data survived confiscation of any single device.
other_false_positives.why: This motive is unsupported: in the key, leaked data is only on RM#2 and the CD-R, and the CD-R was used after the conspirator's "USB device may be easily detected. So, try another method." e-mail (Section 3, Q21).

other_false_positives.quote: Cover image files (24 photographs including amalfi.bmp, barn.gif, boudicca.bmp, cactus.png, and others) were created on RM2's FAT32 partition between 16:55:17 and 16:55:37 UTC, establishing an innocuous appearance for the media.
other_false_positives.why: Q53 states that all other recovered files have no relationship to the scenario, and RM#2 was first connected to the PC on 2015-03-24 09:58 (Q22), so attributing March 23 cover images to the suspect is unsupported.

other_false_positives.quote: 1. 2015-02-27: Root "Secret Project Data" directory on RM1 exFAT deleted
other_false_positives.why: The report lists this as part of "systematic anti-forensic cleanup", but the key has no such action: RM#1 is the authorized company device and the suspect's activity begins 2015-03-22 (Section 3).

Section 3 and Q52 show that the 2015-03-25 11:21-11:22 local launch was to disconnect the Google Drive account (the sign-out deleted sync_config.db and snapshot.db), an anti-forensic step; the Drive exfiltration was on 2015-03-23 at 16:32 (Q30, Q59).

other_false_positives.quote: 4. Searched "anti-forensic+tools" → Implemented file masquerading, deletion, and wiping
other_false_positives.why: Q16 and Q52 date the "anti-forensic tools" search to 2015-03-25 10:46:44, after the masquerading renames (Q23, March 23-24) and the RM#2 deletion (March 24 17:02), so it cannot have led to them.

other_false_positives.quote: "BD-RE Drive (D:) IAMAN CD" with directories D:\de, D:\tr, D:\pd, D:\prop, D:\prog browsed 2015-03-24 19:47-20:44 UTC.
other_false_positives.why: The report offers this as confirmation of RM3 access, but RM#3 was a new CD-R inserted at 16:53 and formatted at 16:53:17 local (20:53:17 UTC, Q33); the D: browsing up to 16:44 local (Q35) was of the first CD-R, which was then reformatted (Section 3).

other_false_positives.quote: D:\de, D:\tr, D:\pd, D:\prop, D:\prog — accessed 2015-03-24 19:47-20:41 (abbreviated versions of the FAT32 partition directories)
other_false_positives.why: D: is the optical drive holding the CD-Rs (Q35, Section 3), not a second partition of a USB stick.

other_false_positives.quote: The last RecentDocs registry write occurred at 15:29:08 UTC, marking the final recorded activity on the system.
other_false_positives.why: The key records later activity: logoff at 11:30:57 and shutdown at 11:31:05 local, i.e. 15:30:57-15:31:05 UTC (Q8, Q12).

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: The timing sequence (anti-forensic cleanup followed by cloud sync) suggests the subject may have synced documents to Google Drive as a supplementary exfiltration vector.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: The March 25 launch was to sign out of Google Drive (Section 3 11:22, Q52); the Drive exfiltration was the 2015-03-23 16:32 upload of happy_holiday.jpg and do_u_wanna_build_a_snow_man.mp3 (Q30, Q59).

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: the destruction of all Google Drive configuration files (sync_config.db, cacerts, snapshot.db) by Eraser
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Q30, Q31, Q48 and Q52 say sync_config.db and snapshot.db were deleted by the Google Drive sign-out at 2015-03-25 11:22:48; Eraser was used to wipe the Desktop temp directory.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: Browser history: 0 windows recovered (consistent with CCleaner clearing browser data)
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: The key says CCleaner was launched and closed after doing nothing (Section 3, 2015-03-25 11:15).

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: no evidence indicates Secret Project Data was transmitted via email. The exfiltration pathway appears to have been exclusively through removable media and potentially cloud storage.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Q45 and Q59 list e-mail as a leakage method: space_and_earth.mp4 (the renamed design_concept.ppt) was attached on 2015-03-23 at 15:19, and Drive share links were sent at 16:38.

labelled_inferences_contradicted.quote: registry analysis shows minimal activity on these accounts, suggesting they may have been diversionary.
labelled_inferences_contradicted.why: Section 3 places the creation of admin11, ITechTeam and temporary in the "Normal ~2015-03-22" setup phase, before the conspirator's first e-mail on 2015-03-23, not as part of the leak.
